subject.title: fix(agents): tighten lsSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer

question: Should the built-in `ls` tool reject fractional `limit` values at schema validation, rather than retaining the currently accepted numeric contract and normalizing values during execution?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically viable, but rejecting values previously accepted by the model-facing schema is an intentional compatibility choice shared with several related tool-schema PRs.

options.title: Accept strict integers after repair
options.body: Rebase the branch, test the registered production schema, refresh exact-head proof, and accept fractional-call rejection as the intended contract.

options.title: Coordinate one schema-hardening change
options.body: Pause this PR and consolidate the related grep, find, bash, and ls contract decisions into one consistently tested change.

options.title: Keep the numeric contract
options.body: Close this PR and retain runtime normalization if backward acceptance of fractional model calls is preferred.

recommendation.title: Accept strict integers after repair
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch, test the registered production schema, refresh exact-head proof, and accept fractional-call rejection as the intended contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the shared built-in agent-tool contract and recent agent-runtime direction.
